literal: That winter he was appointed Chief Secretary of the Sovereign's Office under the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: That winter he was appointed chief secretary in the Heir Apparent's sovereign office.

literal: The next spring, when the Heir Apparent became Grand Commissioner-in-Chief, he was again brought in as Bureau Director of the Commissionerate.
idiomatic: The next spring, when the Heir Apparent became Grand Commissioner-in-Chief, Yang was again made a bureau director of the commissionerate.

literal: In year four, Emperor Gaozu visited the Heavenly Pool at Fenyang; beside the pool he found a stone with raised characters reading "Six, King, Three Rivers."
idiomatic: In the fourth year, Emperor Gaozu visited the Heavenly Pool at Fenyang and found beside it a stone with raised characters: "Six, King, Three Rivers."

literal: Emperor Gaozu asked him alone in the tent what these characters meant; he replied: "Six is the character for 'great king'; a king ought to rule all under Heaven—this is a sign of your destined mandate and token of receiving the mandate."
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu asked him alone in the tent what the inscription meant. Yang answered: "Six is the character for 'great king'; a king ought to rule all under Heaven—this is the omen of your destined mandate."

literal: Now that this stone was obtained at the Heavenly Pool, it may be called Heaven's intent appointing you king—the auspice is beyond words.
idiomatic: Now that this stone came from the Heavenly Pool, it is Heaven appointing you king—the auspice is beyond words.

literal: Emperor Gaozu again asked what "Three Rivers" meant; Xiuzhi said: "The Yellow, Luo, and Yi are called the Three Rivers; some also say the Jing, Wei, and Luo."
idiomatic: The emperor asked what "Three Rivers" meant. Xiuzhi said: "The Yellow, Luo, and Yi are one Three Rivers; some also name the Jing, Wei, and Luo."

literal: The Yellow, Luo, and Yi—that is Luoyang;
idiomatic: The Yellow, Luo, and Yi—that is Luoyang;

literal: the Jing, Wei, and Luo—that is present-day Yong Province.
idiomatic: the Jing, Wei, and Luo—that is present-day Yong Province.

literal: If the Great King receives Heaven's mandate, in the end he ought to rule the whole Guanzhong region."
idiomatic: "If the Great King receives Heaven's mandate, in the end he will hold all of Guanzhong."

literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "When people have nothing better to do they constantly say I intend rebellion; now that they hear this, it will stir more commotion—be careful not to speak rashly."
idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: "Idle tongues are forever saying I mean to rebel; if word of this spreads, the uproar will only grow—do not speak of it lightly."

literal: At the start of Yuanxiang, his military merit at Jing Province was recorded; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xintai County with state-founder rank, fief of six hundred households, and appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and Bureau Director of the Left Department of the People in the Ministry of State Affairs.
idiomatic: At the start of Yuanxiang his Jing Province service was entered in the merit rolls; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xintai with a fief of six hundred households and made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and bureau director of the left people's section.

literal: In the second year of Xinghe he was concurrently Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadency and served as deputy to Cui Changqian of Qinghe on a mission to Liang.
idiomatic: In the second year of Xinghe he was made Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadency and went to Liang as deputy to Cui Changqian of Qinghe.

literal: In the second year of Wuding he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: In the second year of Wuding he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

literal: At the time some wits mocked Xiuzhi, saying: "A ram that has touched the hedge-fence, riding a spirited horse with linked-coin markings, from Jinyang toward Ye, clutching a dossier of names till his hands are full."
idiomatic: Some wits then mocked Xiuzhi in verse: "A ram that has brushed the fence, on a spirited horse marked like linked coins, from Jinyang to Ye, with a roster of names clutched till his hands overflow."

literal: Left Assistant Director of the Ministry Lu Fei submitted his document asking audience; he reported to Emperor Gaozu, who forbade it; an amnesty intervened and he was not punished.
idiomatic: Left assistant director Lu Fei used the lampoon to request an audience; he reported it to Emperor Gaozu, who forbade further action; an amnesty followed and no punishment was imposed.

literal: In the fifth year he was concurrently Chief Steward of Imperial Viands.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he was concurrently chief steward of imperial viands.

literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Household Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Attendant Cavalier of the Yellow Gate, and advanced in rank to General of the Central Army and Chief Rectifier of You Province.
idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made household supervisor of the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Attendant Cavalier of the Yellow Gate and advanced to General of the Central Army and chief rectifier of You Province.

literal: In the eighth year he was concurrently Palace Attendant, bearing credentials and carrying the imperial seal-letter to Bingzhou to urge Xianzu to accept the titles of Chancellor of State and Prince of Qi.
idiomatic: In the eighth year he was concurrently palace attendant, bore credentials, and carried the imperial seal-letter to Bingzhou to urge Xianzu to accept the titles Chancellor of State and Prince of Qi.

literal: At that time Xianzu was about to receive the Wei abdication; he set out from Jinyang and reached Pingyang commandery; because hearts were not yet united he returned for the time being to Bingzhou; fearing leaks, he cut off travel along the roads.
idiomatic: Xianzu was then preparing to receive the Wei abdication; he left Jinyang and reached Pingyang, but because hearts were not yet one he turned back to Bingzhou for the time being; fearing a leak, he cut off traffic on the roads.

literal: Xiuzhi by nature was careless and loose-tongued; when he returned from his mission he spoke of the affair, and everyone in Ye knew.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi was by nature careless and loose-tongued; on his return he spoke of the matter, and all Ye knew.

literal: Later Gao Dezheng reported it; Xianzu was angry but did not yet act.
idiomatic: Later Gao Dezheng reported it; Xianzu was angry but held his hand.

literal: When Qi received the abdication he was appointed Regular Companion of the Fast Cavalry and compiled the Daily Records.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication he was made Regular Companion of the Fast Cavalry and put in charge of the Daily Records.

literal: Before long, for errors in omission in an edict, he was demoted to General of the Valiant Cavalry—the accumulated weight of earlier matters.
idiomatic: Before long, for omissions in an edict, he was demoted to General of the Valiant Cavalry—the accumulated weight of earlier offenses.

literal: Soon, at the time of the abdication rites, he took part in fixing the ritual protocol; separately enfeoffed as Baron of Shiping County with state-founder rank, he held his former post while concurrently serving as army marshal of the Guards.
idiomatic: Soon, during the abdication rites, he helped fix the ritual protocol; he was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Shiping and, retaining his post, concurrently served as army marshal of the Guards.

literal: Later he was appointed Commissioner of Aqueducts, passed through as staff officer of the Minister of Education and vice director of the Secretariat, and soon was made Administrator of Zhongshan.
idiomatic: He was later made commissioner of aqueducts, served as staff officer to the Minister of Education and secretariat vice director, and soon became administrator of Zhongshan.

literal: When Xianzu died, Xiuzhi was summoned to Jinyang to manage the mourning rites.
idiomatic: When Xianzu died, Xiuzhi was summoned to Jinyang to oversee the mourning rites.

literal: In the first year of Ganming he was concurrently Palace Attendant and inspected the capital district.
idiomatic: In the first year of Ganming he was concurrently palace attendant and toured the capital district on inspection.

literal: He was then appointed Grand Master for the Glorious Ceremonial, while retaining the vice-directorship of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand Master for the Glorious Ceremonial while retaining his secretariat vice-directorship.

literal: At the start of Huangjian he held his former post while concurrently serving as Minister of Revenue, was advanced to General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry, and continued as Chief Rectifier of You Province.
idiomatic: At the start of Huangjian he kept his post while concurrently serving as Minister of Revenue, was advanced to General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry, and continued as chief rectifier of You Province.

literal: Emperor Suzong minded the arts of government and often consulted Xiuzhi on methods of rule.
idiomatic: Emperor Suzong attended closely to governance and often asked Xiuzhi for counsel on how to rule.

literal: Xiuzhi answered that clear rewards and punishments, careful management of officials, prohibition of excess and extravagance, and compassion for the people's hardships must come first in governance.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi answered that governance must begin with clear rewards and punishments, careful control of officials, curbing excess and extravagance, and relieving the people's hardships.

literal: The emperor took this deeply to heart.
idiomatic: The emperor took his advice deeply to heart.

literal: During the Daning era he was appointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to the ministries of military affairs and sacrifices.
idiomatic: During Daning he was appointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to the military and sacrifices ministries.

literal: In the third year of Heqing he went out as Governor of Western Yan Province.
idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing he went out as governor of Western Yan Province.

literal: At the start of Tiantong he was recalled as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan and oversaw the national history.
idiomatic: At the start of Tiantong he was recalled as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan and put in charge of the national history.

literal: Xiuzhi in Zhongshan and when governing Western Yan alike had benevolent policies and was cherished by officials and commoners.
idiomatic: Whether in Zhongshan or governing Western Yan, Xiuzhi pursued benevolent policies and won the affection of officials and commoners alike.

literal: After he left office the people erected steles praising his virtue.
idiomatic: After he left office the people raised steles in praise of his virtue.

literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of the Civil Service, drew income from the Yangwu county fief-stipend, was made Honored Companion of the Three Special Ranks, and further given the sovereign's office privilege.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of the Civil Service, drew income from the Yangwu county stipend, was given Honored Companion of the Three Special Ranks, and further granted a sovereign's office.

literal: Xiuzhi knew many precedents and was thoroughly versed in clans; every appointment he made was apt both in talent and in social standing.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi knew precedent inside out and understood clans thoroughly; every man he appointed was fit both in talent and in pedigree.

literal: He was advanced to Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Purple Purse.
idiomatic: He was advanced to Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Purple Purse.

literal: In the first year of Wuping he was appointed Secretariat Director; soon, retaining that post, he was concurrently Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.
idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he was made secretariat director; soon, retaining that post, he was concurrently right vice director of the Ministry of State Affairs.

literal: In the second year he was advanced to Left Grand Master for the Glorious, while concurrently Secretariat Director.
idiomatic: In the second year he was advanced to Left Grand Master for the Glorious while remaining secretariat director.

literal: In the third year he was given the Extraordinary Advancement.
idiomatic: In the third year he was given the rank of Extraordinary Advancement.

literal: In the fifth year he was made regular Secretariat Director; the rest of his posts remained unchanged.
idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made regular secretariat director; his other posts stayed as they were.

literal: Soon, citing age, he sought retirement; he submitted a memorial refusing office; the emperor answered graciously but would not permit it.
idiomatic: Soon, citing age, he sought retirement and submitted a memorial resigning his posts; the emperor answered graciously but would not allow it.

literal: In the sixth year he was made regular Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.
idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made regular right vice director of the Ministry of State Affairs.

literal: Before long he again headed the Secretariat as Director.
idiomatic: Before long he again headed the Secretariat as director.

literal: Xiuzhi by nature was even-tempered and was praised by scholar-friends.
idiomatic: By nature Xiuzhi was even-tempered, and scholar-friends spoke well of him.

literal: In his later years he urged Zu Ting to compile the Imperial Overview; when the book was finished he was given Extraordinary Advancement; when Ting was dismissed he spread word through court that there had been old animosity between them.
idiomatic: In his later years he urged Zu Ting to compile the Imperial Overview; when the book was finished he was given Extraordinary Advancement; when Ting was dismissed he spread word at court that they had long been at odds.

literal: When Deng Changxuan and Yan Zhitui memorialized to establish the Forest of Literature Hall, Zhitui had not intended that elderly eminent men hold posts there; Xiuzhi went along with it and entered together with young court gentlemen and staff officers as editors awaiting edicts.
idiomatic: When Deng Changxuan and Yan Zhitui memorialized to establish the Forest of Literature Hall, Zhitui had not wanted elderly eminent men inside; Xiuzhi went along anyway and entered with young court gentlemen and staff officers as editors awaiting edicts.

literal: Again, when Wei Shou oversaw the history, he drew up the Basic Annals of Emperor Gaozu and took the year of pacifying the Four Barbarians as the founding year of Qi.
idiomatic: Again, while Wei Shou oversaw the history, he drafted the Basic Annals of Emperor Gaozu and took the year of pacifying the Four Barbarians as Qi's founding year.

literal: Shou was in Qi Province and feared the historiographers would alter his intent; he submitted a memorial arguing the point.
idiomatic: Shou was then in Qi Province and feared the historiographers would overturn his intent; he submitted a memorial arguing his case.

literal: Mid-Wuping, Shou returned to court; an edict gathered eminent ministers to deliberate the matter.
idiomatic: Mid-Wuping, Shou returned to court; an edict gathered eminent ministers to debate the question.

literal: Xiuzhi proposed fixing the founding boundary at the Tianbao era.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi argued that the founding era should be fixed at Tianbao.

literal: While Wei Shou still lived, the two positions remained unresolved.
idiomatic: While Wei Shou still lived, the two positions remained deadlocked.

literal: After Shou died he stirred sentiment inside and outside the court until an edict was issued adopting his view.
idiomatic: After Shou died he stirred opinion inside and outside court until an edict was issued in his favor.

literal: Later, when he again headed the Secretariat, he said to people: "I have already been Secretariat Director three times—what use is this title to me?"
idiomatic: Later, when he again headed the Secretariat, he said: "I have already been secretariat director three times—what do I need this for?"

literal: When Longhua returned to Ye, many throughout court received new appointments; Xiuzhi was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan commandery.
idiomatic: When Longhua returned to Ye, many at court received new appointments; Xiuzhi was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan commandery.

literal: He also told those close to him: "I am no slave—why should such an appointment suddenly come to me?"
idiomatic: He also told those close to him: "I am no bondsman's son—why should such an honor fall on me out of nowhere?"

literal: All such matters were deeply despised in the talk of the age.
idiomatic: Such conduct earned him deep contempt in the talk of the age.

literal: Xiuzhi loved learning without tiring, mastered the classics and histories comprehensively; though his writing was not florid, it was canonical and correct.
idiomatic: Xiuzhi loved learning and never tired of it; he mastered the classics and histories broadly; his prose was not ornate, but it was sound and correct.

literal: After Xing and Wei died, he was esteemed as an elder of the former generation.
idiomatic: After Xing Shao and Wei Shou died, he was honored as an elder of the former generation.

literal: Though his rank and fame were high, he received people with open humility and was beloved and respected among the gentry.
idiomatic: Though his rank and fame were high, he met others with open humility and was beloved among the gentry.

literal: When Zhou conquered Qi in the Wuping era, he was summoned together with eighteen others—including Minister of the Civil Service Yuan Yuxiu, Chamberlain of the Guards Li Zuqin, Minister of Revenue Yuan Xiubo, Minister of Justice Sima Youzhi, Minister of Agriculture Cui Dana, Secretariat Director Yuan Wenzong, Regular Companion and Secretariat Vice Director Li Ruo, Regular Companion and Attendant Cavalier Li Xiaozhen, Attendant Cavalier Lu Sidao, Attendant Cavalier Yan Zhitui, Regular Attendant and Secretariat Vice Director Li Delin, Regular Attendant and Secretariat Drafting Officer Lu Yi, Secretariat Vice Director Xue Daohang, and Secretariat Drafting Officers Gao Xinggong, Xin Deyuan, Wang Shao, and Lu Kaiming—to follow the imperial train afterward to Chang'an.
idiomatic: When Zhou conquered Qi in the Wuping era, he was summoned with eighteen others—among them Yuan Yuxiu, Minister of the Civil Service, Li Zuqin, Chamberlain of the Guards, Yuan Xiubo, Minister of Revenue, Sima Youzhi, Minister of Justice, Cui Dana, Minister of Agriculture, Yuan Wenzong, Secretariat Director, and Li Ruo, Li Xiaozhen, Lu Sidao, Yan Zhitui, Li Delin, Lu Yi, Xue Daohang, Gao Xinggong, Xin Deyuan, Wang Shao, and Lu Kaiming—to follow the imperial train to Chang'an.

literal: In something Lu Sidao wrote down he said only that Xiuzhi, Xiaozhen, and Sidao were summoned together—this was his distortion.
idiomatic: In one of Lu Sidao's accounts he named only Xiuzhi, Xiaozhen, and himself as summoned—a deliberate slanting of the record.

literal: Soon he was appointed Honored Companion of the Sovereign's Office, passed through as Palace Secretary, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Honored Companion of the Sovereign's Office and served in turn as palace secretary, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and junior mentor of the Heir Apparent.

literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he was advanced to Upper Honored Companion of the Sovereign's Office and made Governor of He Province.
idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he was advanced to Upper Honored Companion of the Sovereign's Office and made governor of He Province.

literal: In the second year of Sui Kaihuang he left office and died at Luoyang, aged seventy-four.
idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang he left office and died at Luoyang, aged seventy-four.

literal: His collected works ran to thirty juan; he also compiled A Record of Notable Men of You Province, both circulated in his day.
idiomatic: His collected works ran to thirty juan; he also wrote A Record of Notable Men of You Province—both circulated in his lifetime.

literal: His son Bikong, at the end of Wuping, was Bureau Director of Waterways in the Ministry of State Affairs.
idiomatic: His son Bikong, at the end of Wuping, was bureau director of waterways in the Ministry of State Affairs.

literal: Bikong was by nature careless and unrestrained, without literary accomplishment; Xiuzhi nevertheless had him admitted to the Forest of Literature Hall, to the ridicule and scorn of contemporaries.
idiomatic: Bikong was careless and unrestrained and had no literary gift; Xiuzhi nevertheless had him admitted to the Forest of Literature Hall, to the scorn of his contemporaries.

literal: Yuan Yuxiu, courtesy name Shude, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
idiomatic: Yuan Yuxiu, courtesy name Shude, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

literal: He was the son of Fan, Secretariat Director of Wei, and was given in adoption to his uncle Yue.
idiomatic: He was the son of Fan, Wei secretariat director, and was given in adoption to his uncle Yue.

literal: At seven he suffered bereavement; in deportment and ritual observance he was like an adult.
idiomatic: At seven he lost a parent; in deportment and ritual observance he was already like a grown man.

literal: At nine he was invited by the province as chief secretary.
idiomatic: At nine the province invited him to serve as chief secretary.

literal: By nature deep and discerning, pure, sparing in desire, without rivalry toward others, he was deeply known and prized by Cui Xiu of the Ministry of State Affairs.
idiomatic: Deep and discerning by nature, pure and sparing in desire, without rivalry toward others, he won the deep regard of Cui Xiu of the Ministry of State Affairs.

literal: In the Wei's Taichang era he first donned official robes as Libationer of the Western Pavilion of the Grand Tutor's sovereign office.
idiomatic: In the Wei's Taichang era he first entered office as libationer of the Western Pavilion of the Grand Tutor's sovereign office.

literal: At eighteen he headed the rectification office of his native province.
idiomatic: At eighteen he headed the rectification office of his native province.

literal: Soon he was concurrently Director of the Revenue Section in the Ministry and also passed through as director in the military and left-people sections.
idiomatic: Soon he was concurrently director of the revenue section and also served in the military and left-people sections.

literal: At the end of Wuding he was Court Scribe to the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was court scribe to the Heir Apparent.

literal: At the start of Tianbao he was appointed Household Companion to the Heir Apparent and acted as Administrator of Boling with his former title.
idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he was made household companion to the Heir Apparent and acted as administrator of Boling under his existing title.

literal: Within a few years he achieved great reputation and record; near and far praised him.
idiomatic: Within a few years he won a strong reputation; near and far praised his record.

literal: In the eighth year he was concurrently Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse; soon transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Granary, then appointed Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple.
idiomatic: In the eighth year he was concurrently vice director of the Imperial Storehouse; he soon transferred to vice director of the Grand Granary, then became vice director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple.

literal: In the second year of Huangjian he left office on his mother's death; soon an edict restored his former posts, advanced him to General Who Conquers Barbarians and General Who Assists the State, and appointed him Bureau Director of the Civil Service Section.
idiomatic: In the second year of Huangjian he left office to mourn his mother; soon an edict restored his posts, advanced him to General Who Conquers Barbarians and General Who Assists the State, and made him bureau director of the civil service section.

literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, advanced to General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry, and concurrently acted as Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to left chief clerk of the Minister of Education, advanced to General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry, and concurrently acted as imperial censor-in-chief.

literal: Staff Officer Lu Sidao of the Minister of Education privately borrowed four hundred thousand from the treasury to betroth the daughter of Wang Yi of Taiyuan, but the Wang family had already accepted betrothal gifts from Lu Kongwenli; Yuxiu, sitting as chief staff officer and also the state's judicial overseer, knew yet did not impeach, and was reprimanded and removed as censor-in-chief.
idiomatic: Staff officer Lu Sidao of the Minister of Education privately borrowed four hundred thousand from the treasury to betroth Wang Yi's daughter of Taiyuan, though the Wangs had already accepted betrothal gifts from Lu Kongwenli; Yuxiu, as chief staff officer and the state's judicial overseer, knew and did not impeach; he was reprimanded and stripped of the censorate.

literal: Soon he was transferred to Secretariat Director.
idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to secretariat director.

literal: During Tiantong an edict ordered him with the Prince of Zhao commandery Rui and others to deliberate and fix the Five Rites.
idiomatic: During Tiantong an edict ordered him, with the Prince of Zhao commandery Rui and others, to deliberate and fix the Five Rites.

literal: He went out as Governor of Xin Province—that being his native commandery—and people of the time counted it an honor.
idiomatic: He went out as governor of Xin Province—his native commandery—and men of the time counted it an honor.

literal: His government was pure and tranquil; without many words he brought order; from senior officials down to widows, orphans, and the young, all gave him their goodwill.
idiomatic: His rule was pure and tranquil; without many words he brought order; from senior officials down to widows, orphans, and children, all gave him their goodwill.

literal: At the start of Wuping censors went out in force touring the provinces; Liang, Zheng, Yan, and Yu bordered one another on all four sides of Xin Province, and everywhere there were denunciations—but no censor ever reached Xin Province; such was the esteem in which he was held.
idiomatic: At the start of Wuping censors toured the provinces in force; Liang, Zheng, Yan, and Yu lay on every side of Xin, and denunciations arose on all fronts—yet no censor ever reached Xin Province; such was the regard in which he was held.

literal: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, commoners and clergy alike thronged the roads to see him off, some bringing wine and dried meat, weeping and lingering, each vying to escort him far.
idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, commoners and clergy alike filled the roads to see him off, some bringing wine and dried meat, weeping and lingering, each vying to escort him farther.

literal: As it was high summer he feared they would wear themselves out; again and again he halted his horse, took a single cup with whoever offered, to acknowledge their feeling, then declined and sent them back.
idiomatic: It was high summer, and he feared they would weary themselves; again and again he halted his horse, took a single cup from whoever offered one to acknowledge their feeling, then begged them to turn back.

literal: After he returned to the capital, more than seven hundred provincials led by Zheng Bozong asked that a stele be erected for him; they raised several hundred bolts of silk and cloth and entrusted Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Delin to compose the text recording his merit and virtue.
idiomatic: After he reached the capital, more than seven hundred provincials led by Zheng Bozong asked that a stele be raised for him; they collected several hundred bolts of silk and cloth and asked secretariat vice director Li Delin to compose the inscription recording his merit.

literal: The provincial and central offices memorialized upward; an edict replied granting permission.
idiomatic: The provincial and central offices memorialized; an edict granted permission.

literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Justice while still heading his native rectification office; he was transferred to concurrently serve as Minister of the Civil Service and Honored Companion of the Three Special Ranks, and soon his ministry post became regular.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Justice while still heading his native rectification office; he was transferred to concurrently serve as Minister of the Civil Service and Honored Companion of the Three Special Ranks, and soon his ministry post became regular.

literal: Yuxiu from youth was mild and gentle, warm in manner; among those of plain family background he was the most exact in observance and restraint.
idiomatic: From youth Yuxiu was mild and warm in manner; among men of plain family stock he was the most exact in observance and restraint.

literal: As the son of an eminent house he held one brilliant post after another; men of reputation widely regarded him with esteem and credited his judgment of character.
idiomatic: As the son of an eminent house he held one brilliant post after another; men of reputation widely esteemed him and trusted his judgment of character.

literal: In his days in the bureau offices Zhao Yanshen served as Bureau Director of Waterways in the same courtyard; they became fast friends.
idiomatic: In his days in the bureau offices Zhao Yanshen was director of the waterways section in the same courtyard; the two became close friends.

literal: Later Yanshen was culled and suspended, his disciples scattered like wild greens; Yuxiu still, out of old friendship, kept up inquiries and visits.
idiomatic: Later Yanshen was culled and suspended, his disciples scattered like wild greens in winter; Yuxiu still kept up inquiries and visits out of old friendship.
